title: Evolved stress signalling is instructive only at specific concentrations

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Evolved stress signalling is instructive only at specific concentrations

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In the evolved neural cellular automaton, imposing very high stress on an already patterned tissue had no immediate effect on cell states but later altered them, indicating that evolution used stress as a communication code in which stress affects cell behaviour only at specific concentrations.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Pio-Lopez L 2023, The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis › Computational results › Stress is instructive but only at particular levels

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: We conclude that evolution used stress as a communication system using a particular encoding, in which stress level is instructive and has effects on cell behaviour only at specific concentrations.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Pio-Lopez L, Bischof J, LaPalme JV, Levin M, “The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis”, Interface focus (2023), doi:10.1098/rsfs.2022.0072; section “Computational results › Stress is instructive but only at particular levels”. Scope: In silico 2D neural cellular automata evolved for the French flag problem

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2023-goals-07: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.90

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The public code permits a full intervention sweep, not merely inspection of the reported example. The model-specific concentration dependence is therefore currently resolvable.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Sweep imposed stress concentrations and timing in patterned tissues, recording immediate and delayed state transitions. A non-monotonic or threshold-specific dose-response supports concentration coding; uniform responses would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
A delayed response alone does not prove a communication code.

Dose-response should be tested across multiple independently evolved controllers.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Stress level and cell state are measurable in the simulator, so a dose sweep is possible once a tissue exists. The claim reports one qualitative pattern, delayed change after very high stress, and reads it as an evolved code. Without the original networks, re-evolution tests whether some codes are level-specific, not this reported encoding.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Impose a range of constant stress levels on an already patterned tissue and record the immediate and delayed change in cell state. Effects confined to particular concentrations, including no immediate change at a very high level followed by a later change, would support a level-specific code; graded immediate effects at all levels would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
'Specific concentrations' is illustrated rather than given as a full dose-response criterion.

The encoding is a property of particular evolved networks, which are not deposited.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

discriminating power: 0.48
data existence: 0.58
operationalizability: 0.7
analysis feasibility: 0.38
